rows.synonym: Please put together a source-backed market-sizing analysis — total, served, and obtainable market — for an upcoming diagnostic offering. Every statement needs a linked citation, and the projection's underlying guesses should be spelled out with best- and worst-case ranges.
rows.plain: I want a report estimating how big the market is for a new medical-testing product, split into the total market, the part we could reach, and the share we could realistically win. Every claim must trace to its source, and forecast guesses need ranges showing best and worst case.

rows.synonym: I want to construct and model a decoherence-aware quantum circuit targeting the native instruction set of one particular commercial quantum chip, then run a benchmarking test comparing the hardware's actual error rates against the modeled prediction.
rows.plain: I need help designing a quantum computing routine that accounts for hardware noise, built for the built-in operations of one particular company's quantum chip. After modeling it on a computer, I want to run the same routine on the real chip and measure how its actual mistake rate compares to what the model predicted.
rows.expert: Build a noise-aware circuit compiled to a specific vendor processor's native gate set, simulate it, then run hardware characterization to compare measured error rates against the simulated prediction.

rows.synonym: I'm adding a custom capability to Pi and want guidance on registering it, tying into Pi's event framework, and bundling it as an installable add-on so my teammates can use it during their terminal-based coding work.
rows.plain: I'm building a new feature to plug into Pi and need to know three things: how to register it so the system recognizes it, how to connect it to Pi's internal events, and how to package it as an installable add-on so my team can use it in their own terminal coding sessions.
rows.expert: Walk me through registering a custom tool with Pi, wiring it into Pi's event system, and packaging it as an installable extension for team-wide terminal use.

rows.synonym: I'd like to find machine-learning benchmark collections for drug discovery that span drug-target binding, ADMET properties, and molecule-generation problems, then load one using its default task-matched train/test partition and evaluate my predictions with that benchmark's official scoring metric.
rows.plain: I want to find benchmark datasets for testing drug-discovery machine-learning models — covering drug-target binding, how compounds behave in the body, and generating new candidate molecules. I'll load one with its normal training/testing split and score my predictions using that benchmark's own official method.
rows.expert: Surface therapeutics ML benchmark datasets spanning DTI, ADMET, and de novo molecule generation, load one with its canonical train/test split, and score predictions via the benchmark's official evaluator.

rows.synonym: I need to push a set of sequencing files into our DNAnexus project, start up a workflow application against them, and track both job progress and compute spend as it executes.
rows.plain: I need to send a group of sequencing data files into our project on DNAnexus, kick off a processing workflow using those files, and keep an eye on how the job is progressing and how much compute it's costing while it runs.
rows.expert: Batch-upload sequencing files to our DNAnexus project, launch a workflow app against them, and monitor job status and compute spend during execution.

rows.synonym: I have unprocessed flow-cytometry output straight from the instrument and need to examine the channel metadata, extract the event data into an in-memory numeric array for downstream work, and save a new file in the current single-precision variant of the format — compensation and gating aren't required at this stage.
rows.plain: I have raw data files straight off a flow-cytometry machine, with no correction applied yet. I need to check the metadata describing each channel, pull the raw per-event measurements into a numeric array for further coding work, and save a new file in the newer single-precision version of the format. I don't need to apply compensation or sort cells into groups yet.
rows.expert: Parse raw instrument-native cytometry files, inspect channel metadata, pull event data into an array for downstream processing, and re-save as the modern single-precision file-format variant — no compensation or gating yet.

rows.synonym: I've collected some early experimental observations and would like help converting them into clearly written candidate hypotheses, each with competing explanations and predictions that could be tested, along with an analysis plan ready for preregistration — without assuming my initial guess is correct.
rows.plain: I have some early results from an experiment and want help turning them into a few clearly worded possible explanations, each paired with alternative explanations and predictions I could test. I also want an analysis plan detailed enough to lock in ahead of time, without treating my first guess as the answer.
rows.expert: Convert preliminary observations into clearly stated candidate hypotheses with rival explanations and testable predictions, plus a preregistration-ready analysis plan, without privileging the initial hypothesis.

rows.synonym: I have a folder holding a mix of DOCX documents, PPTX slide decks, and CSV files that need converting into clean Markdown text so I can index them for a retrieval-augmented-generation pipeline. I don't need bounding boxes or page images — just readable, structured text.
rows.plain: I have a folder of different file types — word-processor documents, slide-deck presentations, and spreadsheet-style CSV files — that I need turned into clean, plain structured text with simple formatting markers, so I can index the contents for a system that retrieves text to feed into a generation pipeline. I don't need layout coordinates or images of the pages, just readable text.
rows.expert: Convert a mixed folder of DOCX, PPTX, and CSV files into clean Markdown for RAG indexing — structured text only, no bounding boxes or page images needed.

rows.synonym: I have an in-silico collection of several thousand candidate molecules and need to remove any that break Lipinski's rule of five or Veber's rules, while flagging anything carrying PAINS or other structural-alert substructures, ahead of prioritizing compounds for synthesis.
rows.plain: I have a computer-based list of a few thousand possible drug-like molecules. I want to remove any that fail standard drug-likeness rules covering things like molecular weight, fat solubility, and flexibility, and separately flag any molecules containing chemical substructures known to cause false positives or other red-flag patterns in lab assays — all before we decide which compounds to actually make.
rows.expert: Filter the virtual library against Lipinski Ro5 and Veber criteria, and flag PAINS/structural-alert substructures, ahead of synthesis prioritization.

rows.synonym: I need to design a bespoke microplate rack that fits precisely to our plate reader's measurements and export it as a STEP file, ready to send to a 3D printer.
rows.plain: I want to design a custom holder or tray for lab microplates that fits exactly to the size of our plate-reading instrument, then save the design as a STEP-format 3D model file so it's ready to be 3D printed.
rows.expert: Design a custom microplate holder matched to our plate reader's footprint and export a print-ready STEP file for additive manufacturing.

rows.synonym: I'm developing a graph neural network for node classification on a large, multi-type graph, built from message-passing layers, and I need help with mini-batch neighbor sampling so that training can scale to a graph too large to hold in memory at once.
rows.plain: I'm building a neural network that works on graph-structured data, aiming to label nodes in a large graph with several different kinds of nodes and edges, passing information along connections layer by layer. Since the whole graph is too big for memory at once, I need help sampling small batches of neighboring nodes so I can train in pieces.
rows.expert: Building a heterogeneous GNN for node classification with message-passing layers; need mini-batch neighbor sampling to scale training beyond memory-resident graphs.

rows.synonym: After a processing step, my BED-file coordinates no longer match my VCF positions — could there be an off-by-one shift somewhere — and how can I verify my variant calls sit on the right reference genome build before checking them against ClinVar?
rows.plain: After one pipeline step, my interval-file position ranges no longer line up with my variant-call file's positions — I suspect a shift of exactly one base somewhere. I also want to check that my called variants are mapped to the correct reference-genome version before comparing them to a known variant database.
rows.expert: Post-pipeline, BED intervals and VCF positions disagree — suspect an off-by-one coordinate shift — and I need to verify genome-build concordance before cross-referencing against ClinVar.

rows.synonym: I want to train a reinforcement-learning agent using an established, ready-made algorithm such as PPO or SAC, on a standard simulation environment built to the usual RL interface, without hand-coding the training loop or policy network myself.
rows.plain: I want to train an AI agent that learns through trial and reward, using a well-known, already-implemented algorithm like PPO or SAC, in a standard simulated environment following a common reinforcement-learning interface. I don't want to write the training loop or the policy network myself.
rows.expert: Train an RL agent with an off-the-shelf PPO or SAC implementation on a standard reinforcement-learning environment interface, without hand-rolling the training loop or policy network.

rows.synonym: I have a shapefile containing county boundary polygons and a CSV listing clinic locations by latitude and longitude, and I need to spatially match each clinic to the county polygon that contains it, then reproject all the data into one consistent coordinate reference system.
rows.plain: I have a geographic file outlining county borders as shapes, and a spreadsheet listing clinic locations by latitude and longitude. I need to determine which county shape each clinic falls inside, attach that information, then convert all the location data to use one consistent map projection and coordinate system.
rows.expert: Spatially join clinic point locations (CSV lat/lon) to containing county polygons (shapefile), then reproject both layers to a common CRS.

rows.synonym: Before modeling begins, I'd like an anonymized profile of my CSV data set — covering missing-data patterns, potential train/test leakage, and how outlier sensitivity shifts across different transformations — compiled into a thorough, structured report.
rows.plain: Before building any models, I want an overview of my spreadsheet-style dataset with identifying details removed — covering where data is missing, whether information leaks between training and testing sets, and how sensitive extreme values are to different transformations. I want this pulled into one careful, well-organized report.
rows.expert: Generate a redacted EDA profile of the CSV — missingness patterns, train/test leakage risk, and outlier sensitivity across transformations — as a structured report.

rows.synonym: For weeks I've been repeating the same multi-step research routine on my machine, and I'd like you to look over my recent on-screen activity — recorded locally and never transmitted without my explicit consent — to suggest a reusable workflow for it.
rows.plain: For weeks I've done the same multi-step research task repeatedly on my computer. I want you to look back at a recording of my recent screen activity — staying on my own machine, never sent elsewhere unless I say so — and use it to suggest a repeatable process I could follow instead.
rows.expert: Review recent locally-captured screen activity (not transmitted without consent) from a repeated multi-step research routine and propose a reusable workflow.

rows.synonym: I need to write a manufacturer-independent liquid-handling protocol in Python that runs on either our Hamilton STAR or our Tecan EVO, and simulate it offline first with a visual deck layout before any real run.
rows.plain: I need to write one liquid-handling procedure in the Python language that works on two different brands of lab liquid-handling robot we own, without changing the code for each. Before running it on real equipment, I want to test it on the computer first and see a visual picture of the robot's deck layout.
rows.expert: Write a vendor-agnostic Python liquid-handling protocol targeting both the Hamilton STAR and Tecan EVO, with offline simulation and a visual deck preview before physical execution.

rows.synonym: I need to take a list of UniProt accession numbers, translate them into KEGG pathway IDs, and retrieve both pathway and Gene Ontology annotations — all via one unified interface, rather than managing separate clients for each database.
rows.plain: I have a list of protein identifiers from a standard protein database, and want to convert them into pathway identifiers from a standard pathway database, then retrieve pathway information and standardized gene-function annotations. I want one consistent way of asking for the data, instead of a different tool per database.
rows.expert: Map UniProt accessions to KEGG pathway IDs and retrieve pathway/GO annotations through one unified interface rather than per-database clients.

rows.synonym: I'd like a refined single-page visual overview — icons, headline figures, a tidy layout — covering '5 key benefits of a Mediterranean diet,' backed by accurately researched numbers and a colorblind-friendly palette, ready for posting on social media.
rows.plain: I want a polished, single-page graphic summarizing five key benefits of a Mediterranean-style diet, using icons, a few standout statistics, and a clean layout. The statistics need to be accurate and researched, colors must work for colorblind viewers, and it should be finished and ready to post on social media.
rows.expert: Produce a one-page infographic on '5 key benefits of a Mediterranean diet' — icons, key stats, clean layout, colorblind-safe palette, researched figures — social-media ready.

rows.synonym: I need a system that records the complete processing history of my single-cell RNA-seq data — which script generated which version of each annotated data object — and lets me query and check them against standard ontologies for cell type and tissue.
rows.plain: I want a system that keeps track of the full history of how each of my single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was produced — which script created which version of the resulting data object. I also want to search through that history and check the recorded cell-type and tissue labels against standard, agreed-upon reference vocabularies.
rows.expert: Need full provenance tracking for scRNA-seq processing — script-to-artifact-version lineage for each annotated cell-by-gene data object — plus queryable validation against standard cell-type and tissue ontologies.

rows.synonym: Our clinical staff has already settled on a patient's treatment plan, and I need to turn that decision into a structured document with goals, milestones, and a clear audit trail leading back to the approving clinician. I'm not making any clinical judgment myself.
rows.plain: The clinical team has already made the decision about how to treat a patient — I'm not involved in that choice at all. What I need is to take their already-finished decision and put it into an organized record that lists the goals, the checkpoints along the way, and a clear record of which clinician signed off on it.
rows.expert: Format an already-decided clinical intervention plan into a structured record — goals, checkpoints, and an audit trail to the approving clinician — with no clinical decision-making on my part.

rows.synonym: We're getting ready for an ISO 13485 quality-management-system audit at our medical-device company and need to arrange our controlled documents, risk-management file, and CAPA records into a structured evidence package ahead of human review.
rows.plain: We're getting ready for a quality-system audit under a specific medical-device manufacturing standard, and I need to gather our controlled documents, our risk-management records, and our records of corrective and preventive actions into one organized package of evidence, ready for a person to review before the audit.
rows.expert: Compile controlled documents, the risk management file, and CAPA records into a structured evidence package ahead of an ISO 13485 QMS audit, pending human review.

rows.synonym: I'm resubmitting an NIH R01 grant application after the review panel flagged its innovation as weak, and I need help tightening the specific aims and significance narrative, along with the budget justification, ahead of the next deadline.
rows.plain: I'm sending back a revised major national research-grant proposal, after reviewers said it wasn't innovative enough. I need help making the stated goals and significance argument more compelling, and improving the written budget justification, all before the upcoming deadline.
rows.expert: Resubmitting an R01 after a weak-innovation critique from study section; need the specific aims, significance narrative, and budget justification sharpened before deadline.

rows.synonym: I've taken over a codebase of numerical .m scripts and need help checking them for correctness, plus figuring out whether parts of it can safely be moved to run on a free, open-source interpreter instead.
rows.plain: I've taken over someone else's numerical scripts, written in a scripting language used for math and engineering, and need help checking whether the code is correct, plus figuring out whether some of it could safely switch to a free, open-source alternative interpreter.
rows.expert: Inherited a .m-script codebase; need a correctness review and an assessment of whether parts can safely migrate to a free, open-source interpreter.

rows.synonym: I need to model the Lindblad master-equation evolution of an open quantum system — a two-level atom coupled to a lossy bath — and also perform quantum-trajectory unraveling to generate single-shot measurement records.
rows.plain: I want to simulate how a simple two-level quantum system behaves when coupled to an environment causing it to lose energy over time, using the standard equation for this kind of open-system decay. I also want a version producing individual, single-shot measurement outcomes, not just averaged behavior.
rows.expert: Simulate Lindblad master-equation dynamics for a two-level atom coupled to a dissipative bath, and run quantum-trajectory unraveling for single-shot measurement records.

rows.synonym: I have a pair of particle-seeded flow images from a wind-tunnel test and need to cross-correlate interrogation windows to derive the 2D velocity field, then check for and replace spurious vectors before calculating vorticity.
rows.plain: I have two images taken moments apart, showing tracer particles moving through airflow in a wind-tunnel test. I need to compare matching patches between the images to find how the flow moved in two dimensions, check the velocity map for wrong values and fix them, then calculate local rotation.
rows.expert: Cross-correlate interrogation windows from the paired particle-seeded flow images to extract the 2D velocity field, validate/replace spurious vectors, then compute vorticity.

rows.synonym: I want to produce new protein sequence variants by inpainting masked regions of a partial sequence using a multimodal generative protein model, then obtain a predicted all-atom structure for the finished sequence.
rows.plain: I want to create new protein sequence variants by having a model fill in blanked-out sections of a partial sequence, using a model that accepts more than one type of input. Then, for the completed sequence, I want a predicted three-dimensional structure including the position of every atom.
rows.expert: Generate novel sequence variants by masked-region inpainting with a multimodal generative protein model, then predict all-atom structure for the completed sequence.

rows.synonym: I need to automatically retrieve every item and PDF attachment from a shared Zotero group library, sort them by collection, and export the metadata for a systematic review.
rows.plain: I need something that automatically goes through a shared reference library on Zotero, pulling every entry and its attached PDF, sorting everything by collection, then exporting the descriptive metadata for a systematic literature review.
rows.expert: Programmatically pull all items and PDF attachments from a shared Zotero group library, organize by collection, and export metadata for a systematic review.

rows.synonym: Before I kick off this big local computation, could you verify how much processing power, memory, and graphics-processing capacity I actually have available in this environment, including any scheduling or containerization limits I might be operating under?
rows.plain: Before I start a big computing job on this machine, can you check exactly how much processing power, working memory, and graphics-card capacity is actually available to me right now, including any limits that might be imposed by a job scheduler or by running inside a resource-limited container?
rows.expert: Before launching this compute-heavy job, check actual available CPU, RAM, and GPU in this environment, including any scheduler- or container-imposed resource limits.

rows.synonym: I have a protein structure and a set of candidate small molecules given as SMILES strings, and I want to predict the most probable 3D binding pose for each one, along with a confidence score indicating how much to trust that pose, as part of a virtual screening effort.
rows.plain: I have the 3D shape of a protein and a list of small candidate molecules written in a standard chemical-structure notation. For each, I want a prediction of how it most likely orients when bound to the protein in three dimensions, plus a score for how confident I should be in that prediction, as part of a computer-based screening process.
rows.expert: Predict 3D binding poses and pose-confidence scores for a SMILES-form candidate library against a given protein structure, as part of a virtual screen.

rows.synonym: I'm drafting the methods and results portions of a manuscript and need every quantitative statement to trace back to verified evidence, so I don't unintentionally invent a p-value or reference, all while keeping the unpublished data private from any outside service.
rows.plain: I'm writing the parts of a research paper describing how the study was done and what was found. Every number I state needs checking against verified evidence, so I don't accidentally invent a statistical result or a nonexistent reference. None of my not-yet-published data should be shared with any outside service.
rows.expert: Drafting methods/results with every numeric claim traced to verified evidence to prevent fabricated p-values or citations, while keeping unpublished data off any external service.

rows.synonym: I ran a study comparing three treatment groups and need to choose the appropriate statistical test, verify that my data actually satisfies that test's assumptions, calculate effect sizes, and write up the results in a way that would hold up under a journal reviewer's scrutiny.
rows.plain: I compared three treatment groups in an experiment. I need help picking the right statistical test, checking whether my data fits that test's required conditions, calculating how large the differences between groups really are, then writing this up carefully enough that a journal reviewer wouldn't find a weak spot to criticize.
rows.expert: Select the appropriate test for a three-arm comparison, verify its assumptions, compute effect sizes, and write up results to withstand journal peer review.

rows.synonym: I have ChIP-seq BAM files from treated and control samples and need to produce normalized coverage tracks, assess sample correlation and enrichment quality, and construct a heatmap of signal centered on transcription start sites.
rows.plain: I have aligned sequencing files from a chromatin immunoprecipitation experiment, covering treated and control samples. I need normalized tracks showing genome-wide read coverage, a check of sample correlation and signal enrichment, and a heatmap showing signal around gene-transcription starting points.
rows.expert: Generate normalized coverage tracks from ChIP-seq BAM files (treatment vs. control), assess sample correlation and enrichment QC, and build a TSS-centered signal heatmap.

rows.synonym: I have a list of significantly up- and down-regulated genes from a differential-expression analysis and want to test which KEGG and Reactome pathways come up over-represented, plus run a full ranked gene-set enrichment analysis using the test statistic, and produce a clean dotplot.
rows.plain: I have a list of genes that came out significantly more or less active from a gene-expression comparison. I want to test which pathways from two standard pathway databases are over-represented in this list, plus run a ranked version using every gene's test statistic, and make a clean dot-style chart of the results.
rows.expert: Run over-representation analysis against KEGG/Reactome on the DE gene list, plus ranked GSEA on the test statistic, and produce a clean dotplot.

rows.synonym: I need a publication-ready diagram of a signaling pathway, with labeled receptors and downstream effectors, for a figure in my paper. I have no design skills and don't want to construct it by hand — I'd rather describe it in words and receive a finished image.
rows.plain: I need a nice-looking, publication-ready picture showing a cell-signaling pathway, with the receptors and the molecules further down the chain clearly labeled, to use as a figure in my paper. I don't know how to design graphics, and I don't want to build the image manually myself. Instead, I want to describe what should be in it using words, and have a finished image made for me.
rows.expert: Need a publication-quality signaling-pathway diagram with labeled receptors and downstream effectors, generated from a text description rather than manually built.

rows.synonym: I'm conducting a mouse study and want to merge body-weight loss, temperature readings, and clinical scores into one per-animal severity score, benchmarked against a reference group of animals with known burden levels, then predict which animals are trending toward a humane endpoint before they arrive there.
rows.plain: I'm running a mouse experiment and want to combine weight loss, body temperature, and clinical scores into one number per animal reflecting how unwell it is, calibrated against a reference group with known suffering levels. Then I want to predict ahead of time which animals are heading toward needing humane euthanasia, before they arrive there.
rows.expert: Combine weight loss, temperature, and clinical scores into a per-animal composite severity score benchmarked to known-burden reference animals, then forecast trajectories toward humane-endpoint criteria.

rows.synonym: I have a dataset of molecules encoded as graphs and want to pretrain a self-supervised graph-representation model on them, then fine-tune it for property prediction and also attempt a retrosynthesis-prediction task, all within one consistent graph-learning framework.
rows.plain: I have molecules represented as graphs of atoms and bonds, and want to first train a model on them without labeled targets, learning general structure. Then I want to adjust that model to predict chemical properties, and separately try predicting which starting materials could make a target molecule — all within one consistent graph-based setup.
rows.expert: Self-supervised pretrain a graph representation model on molecular graphs, then fine-tune for property prediction and retrosynthesis prediction within one consistent graph-learning framework.

rows.synonym: I'm designing a screening study covering six factors that might influence my assay's yield, and I want to set up a fractional-factorial layout with a randomized run order so the effects aren't confounded, before any data collection begins.
rows.plain: I'm planning an experiment testing six factors that might affect my assay's yield. I want a reduced set of test combinations rather than every possible combination, with randomized run order so different factors' effects don't get mixed up, and I want this plan finished before collecting any data.
rows.expert: Design a six-factor fractional-factorial screen with randomized run order to avoid confounding, prior to data collection.

rows.synonym: I need to build an editable, macro-free PPTX conference poster using my approved figures, abstract text, and citations, and confirm it's print- and accessibility-compliant before handing it off for review.
rows.plain: I need to build a conference poster in an editable slide-based file format with no embedded macros, pulling in my already-approved figures, abstract text, and citations. Before sending it for review, it needs to be ready for printing and meet accessibility standards.
rows.expert: Build an editable, macro-free .pptx conference poster from approved figures, abstract, and citations, verified print- and accessibility-compliant before handoff for review.

rows.synonym: I have raw LC-MS/MS proteomics spectra and need to detect and quantify peptide features across several runs, align their retention times, merge them into a consensus feature table, and produce a wide intensity matrix for downstream statistical analysis.
rows.plain: I have raw mass-spectrometry proteomics data across several runs. I need to identify and measure peptide features in each run, adjust for slight retention-time shifts between runs, combine everything into one shared feature table, then produce a table where rows are features and columns are each sample's intensity.
rows.expert: Detect/quantify peptide features across LC-MS/MS runs, align retention times, build a consensus feature table, and export a wide intensity matrix for downstream stats.

rows.synonym: I need a photorealistic illustration of a glowing deep-sea jellyfish for our outreach flyer, and I'd also like the background lighting adjusted on a reference photo I already have.
rows.plain: I need a realistic-looking picture of a jellyfish that glows in the dark, living deep in the ocean, for a public-outreach flyer. Separately, I have a photo I'd like to keep, but want its background lighting changed.
rows.expert: Need a photorealistic bioluminescent deep-sea jellyfish illustration for an outreach flyer, plus a background-lighting edit on an existing reference photo.

rows.synonym: I want to plan an embedding run over my collection of BED files using a region-embedding approach similar to word-embedding methods, and confirm that my tokenizer vocabulary is actually compatible with the pretrained model before committing to training.
rows.plain: I want to plan a run turning each of my genomic-interval files into numeric vector representations, using an approach that treats genomic regions like word-embedding methods treat words. Before committing to training, I want to check my tokenizer's vocabulary is compatible with the pretrained model.
rows.expert: Plan a region-embedding run over the BED file collection and verify tokenizer-vocabulary compatibility with the pretrained model before committing to training.

rows.synonym: I need up-to-date figures on the U.S. national debt and recent Treasury-securities auction results, drawn directly from an official government data source rather than estimated from memory, for a report I'm writing on federal borrowing trends.
rows.plain: I need the latest actual numbers for how much debt the U.S. federal government currently holds, along with results from recent auctions of government debt securities. These numbers need to come directly from an official government source, not be guessed or recalled from memory, since I'm writing a report about trends in federal borrowing.
rows.expert: Need current U.S. national debt figures and recent Treasury auction results pulled live from an official government source, not approximated from memory, for a federal-borrowing-trends report.

rows.synonym: I need to locate and download a public set of lung CT scans in DICOM format from the National Cancer Institute's public cancer-imaging archive, for use in training a radiology AI model, and verify the data's license terms.
rows.plain: I need a publicly available collection of lung CT scan images, in the standard medical-imaging format, from a well-known government cancer-imaging repository, to train a radiology AI system. I also need to check what the license terms allow me to do with that data.
rows.expert: Source and download a public lung CT DICOM cohort from NCI's cancer imaging archive for a radiology AI training set, and verify licensing terms.

rows.synonym: My dataframe-based processing script runs out of memory on a dataset far larger than my laptop's RAM, and I want to scale the same table-style operations across multiple cores or a small cluster, without rewriting the underlying logic from scratch.
rows.plain: My script for processing table-organized data runs out of memory on a dataset much bigger than my laptop's RAM. I want to spread the same table-based operations across multiple processor cores, or a small group of connected machines, without rewriting the underlying logic from scratch.
rows.expert: Dataframe-style ETL script OOMs on a dataset exceeding local RAM; need the same logic scaled across cores or a small cluster without a rewrite.

rows.synonym: I have whole-slide H&E-stained histology images and want to predict spatial gene expression for a specified gene list across the tissue directly from the images, without actually running a spatial-sequencing assay.
rows.plain: I have large, whole-slide microscope images of tissue stained with a standard two-color histology stain. I want to predict, directly from these images, how strongly a specific list of genes is expressed at different spots across the tissue, without actually running a real spatial gene-expression sequencing experiment.
rows.expert: Predict spatial gene expression for a target gene list directly from whole-slide H&E images, in lieu of running an actual spatial transcriptomics assay.

rows.synonym: I need to track down the DOI for a paper for which I only have partial citation details, check whether it's open access, retrieve the full text, and identify which later papers cited it, across whichever scholarly databases have it indexed.
rows.plain: I only have part of the citation for an academic paper and need to find its unique identifier using what I have. I then need to check if it's freely readable, get the full text, and find which later papers cited it, across whatever academic databases list it.
rows.expert: Resolve the DOI from partial citation details, check OA status, retrieve full text, and pull forward citations, across whichever indexing databases carry the record.

rows.synonym: I'm completing a GEO submission's tissue and cell-type fields and need to convert free-text labels like 'PBMC' and 'left ventricle' into validated ontology term IDs, plus check whether a CURIE already present in my metadata table has become obsolete.
rows.plain: I'm filling out a public gene-expression database submission's tissue and cell-type fields. Some entries are informal text, like 'PBMC' or 'left ventricle,' and I need each matched to a validated identifier from a standard reference vocabulary. I also need to check whether an identifier already in my table has been marked outdated.
rows.expert: Resolve free-text tissue/cell-type labels (e.g. 'PBMC', 'left ventricle') to validated ontology term IDs for a GEO submission, and check an existing CURIE for obsolescence.

rows.synonym: I have raw ECG and skin-conductance recordings from a physiology experiment and need to preprocess them, detect events, and calculate heart-rate variability along with other complexity metrics, all within a reproducible pipeline.
rows.plain: I have raw heart-electrical-activity and skin-conductance recordings from a physiology experiment. I need to clean the raw data, detect specific events, then calculate heartbeat-timing variability and other complexity measures — all through a pipeline giving the same results every rerun.
rows.expert: Preprocess raw ECG/EDA recordings, detect events, and compute HRV plus other complexity metrics in a reproducible pipeline.

rows.synonym: I need to solve a differential equation symbolically, arriving at an exact closed-form expression rather than a numerical approximation, then convert that expression into compilable code I can drop directly into a simulation.
rows.plain: I need to solve an equation involving rates of change using exact algebraic methods, so I end up with a precise formula rather than an approximate numerical answer. Then I need that formula turned into code that can be compiled, ready to insert directly into a simulation program.
rows.expert: Solve the ODE/PDE symbolically for an exact closed-form solution (not a numerical approximation), then code-generate compilable output for direct use in a simulation.

rows.synonym: I have Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and need to compute NDVI from its spectral bands, then perform watershed delineation and hydrological terrain analysis on a raster elevation model.
rows.plain: I have satellite images from an Earth-imaging mission and want to calculate a vegetation-greenness index using its color bands. Then, using a grid-based elevation dataset, I want to map drainage basin boundaries and how water flows across the terrain.
rows.expert: Compute NDVI from Sentinel-2 bands, then run watershed delineation and hydrological terrain analysis on a DEM raster.

rows.synonym: I want to benchmark several different approaches for converting my SMILES library into numeric features for a QSAR model — including both classical fingerprints and pretrained transformer embeddings — to determine which representation best predicts activity.
rows.plain: I want to compare several ways of turning my chemical-structure text strings into numeric features for a structure-activity model — including traditional bit-pattern fingerprints and newer representations from a pretrained deep-learning model — to see which predicts biological activity best.
rows.expert: Benchmark classical fingerprint vs. pretrained transformer-embedding featurizations of the SMILES library for QSAR activity prediction.

rows.synonym: I want to run energy minimization followed by a production simulation of a protein-ligand complex, then calculate RMSD and RMSF from the resulting trajectory to evaluate binding stability.
rows.plain: I want to first settle a protein-drug complex into a low-energy shape, then run the dynamics simulation. From the motion data, I want to measure how much the structure moves and how much its parts wiggle, to judge binding stability.
rows.expert: Run energy minimization and production MD on the protein-ligand complex, then compute RMSD/RMSF from the trajectory to assess binding stability.

rows.synonym: I'm about to validate a new HPLC assay for a drug product and need to design the study along with acceptance criteria for linearity, accuracy, precision, and detection/quantitation limits, all under the appropriate regulatory framework, before any data collection begins.
rows.plain: I'm about to formally verify a new liquid-chromatography lab test for a drug product. I need to plan the study and set pass/fail criteria for proportional response, accuracy, repeatability, and the smallest reliably measured amounts — under the correct regulatory rules, before gathering any data.
rows.expert: Design the validation study and acceptance criteria (linearity, accuracy, precision, LOD/LOQ) for a new HPLC assay under the applicable regulatory framework, prior to data collection.

rows.synonym: I want to submit a cell-free protein-expression validation run to Ginkgo Bioworks' automated wet-lab platform and receive HiBiT luminescence quantification results back, without performing the bench work myself.
rows.plain: I want to send a test run for making protein without living cells, using Ginkgo Bioworks' automated laboratory service, and get back a light-based readout measuring how much protein was made, without doing any hands-on lab work myself.
rows.expert: Submit a cell-free expression validation run to Ginkgo Bioworks' automated platform and retrieve HiBiT luminescence readout, with no bench work on my end.

rows.synonym: I'm putting together a methods report and want to represent my data-processing pipeline as a text-based diagram embedded directly inside a Markdown file, so that it produces clean differences under version control and displays natively on the code-hosting platform, rather than as an image I'd need to regenerate each time.
rows.plain: I'm writing a methods report and want my data-processing steps drawn as a plain-text diagram, placed inside a Markdown document. That way the version-tracking system shows clean differences when text changes, and the diagram displays properly on the website hosting my code, without redrawing an image every time something changes.
rows.expert: Represent the pipeline as a text-based diagram embedded in Markdown, so it diffs cleanly under version control and renders natively on the code-hosting platform instead of a regenerated image.

rows.synonym: I have raw DICOM scans from an MRI study spanning multiple subjects and sessions, and need to convert them into a standardized, validated directory structure with proper JSON metadata sidecar files, before sharing the dataset on a public imaging repository.
rows.plain: I have raw brain-scan images, in the standard medical-imaging format, from an MRI study across several people and sessions. I need to reorganize these into a standard, checkable folder structure, with small JSON files holding each scan's metadata, before sharing the dataset on a public imaging repository.
rows.expert: Convert raw multi-subject, multi-session MRI DICOM data into a standardized, validated directory layout with JSON metadata sidecars, ahead of public repository deposition.

rows.synonym: I'm combining single-cell RNA-seq data from several sequencing batches and want a deep generative model that corrects for batch effects while providing an uncertainty-aware differential-expression test between conditions — something I can later use to project newly collected cells onto the same reference latent space.
rows.plain: I'm combining single-cell RNA sequencing data collected across several different sequencing runs, which each introduce their own technical differences. I want a deep-learning model that can remove those technical differences while still letting me test, with a sense of statistical confidence, which genes differ between experimental conditions. Later on, I also want to place newly collected cells into that same learned reference space, without retraining everything from scratch.
rows.expert: Need a deep generative model for scRNA-seq batch integration with uncertainty-aware differential expression testing between conditions, supporting later reference-mapping of newly collected cells into the same latent space.

rows.synonym: I'm moving a slow dataframe-based ETL script to a tool that offers lazy query optimization and out-of-core streaming, so it can process a dataset too large for memory, using an Arrow-based expression interface.
rows.plain: I have a slow table-based data-processing script that can't handle a dataset bigger than memory. I want to move it to something that computes only what's needed and streams from disk instead of loading everything at once, using an interface built on a modern columnar data format.
rows.expert: Migrating a dataframe-style ETL script to lazy-evaluated, out-of-core execution over an Arrow-based expression API, to handle data that exceeds available memory.

rows.synonym: I have multivariate sensor time-series data from a group of machines and need to classify each recording into one of several failure-mode categories, plus flag anomalous segments and change points, all through a consistent fit/predict-style estimator interface.
rows.plain: I have sensor readings with several measurements over time from a set of machines. I need to sort each recording into one of several failure categories, and separately flag unusual stretches and shift points, through one consistent, standard-style modeling interface common in machine-learning libraries.
rows.expert: Classify multivariate sensor time series into failure-mode categories, plus flag anomalous segments and change points, via a consistent fit/predict-style estimator interface.

rows.synonym: I'm designing a new study and need to determine how many participants to enroll in order to achieve 80% power for detecting a clinically meaningful effect, so I can justify the sample size in my IRB submission and grant application.
rows.plain: I'm planning a new research study and need to figure out how many people I should recruit so that I have an 80% chance of detecting a real difference that would actually matter clinically, if one exists. I need this number so I can explain and defend my sample size to the ethics review board and in my grant application.
rows.expert: Determine enrollment needed for 80% power to detect a clinically meaningful effect, to justify sample size for IRB submission and the grant application.

rows.synonym: I need to build a conference research poster using a professional-grade typesetting system, with a multi-column layout sized for a standard A0 board, incorporating a few AI-generated schematic figures I'll produce separately.
rows.plain: I need a conference research poster made with a markup-based document typesetting system rather than a drag-and-drop tool, with a clean multi-column layout sized for a standard large poster board, incorporating a few schematic figures I'll generate separately using AI.
rows.expert: Build an A0 conference poster in a professional multi-column typesetting-system layout, incorporating separately generated AI schematic figures.

rows.synonym: Our lab uses LabArchives as its electronic notebook system, and I need help writing a script that authenticates using signed requests and retrieves a list of recent notebook entries and inventory items through its API.
rows.plain: Our lab keeps its research notes in an electronic lab notebook system called LabArchives. I need help writing a script that logs in using cryptographically signed requests, then automatically pulls down a list of recent notebook entries and inventory items through the system's programmatic interface.
rows.expert: Write a script that authenticates to LabArchives via signed requests and pulls recent notebook entries and inventory items through its API.

rows.synonym: I have several h5ad files from separate single-cell experiments and need to merge them into one sparse-matrix-backed object that keeps all per-cell and per-gene metadata correctly aligned, without running any clustering or normalization yet.
rows.plain: I have several single-cell data files, each from a separate experiment, in a standard single-cell storage format. I need to merge them into one combined object backed by sparse-matrix storage, keeping per-cell and per-gene metadata correctly matched. I don't want clustering or normalization run yet.
rows.expert: Merge multiple h5ad files into one sparse-matrix-backed object with per-cell and per-gene metadata correctly aligned, with no clustering or normalization yet.

rows.synonym: I have calibration certificates and repeatability measurements for a lab instrument and need to construct a full measurement-uncertainty budget with a defensible coverage factor, while also verifying that my unit conversions between the raw sensor output and the final reported value are dimensionally correct.
rows.plain: I have official calibration documents and repeated-measurement data for lab equipment. I need to build a complete accounting of measurement-error sources, combine them properly, and pick a well-justified multiplier setting my confidence level. I also want to check that converting raw sensor units to final reported units stays dimensionally consistent.
rows.expert: Build a full measurement uncertainty budget with a defensible coverage factor from calibration and repeatability data, and verify dimensional consistency of the raw-to-reported unit conversions.

rows.synonym: I have raw droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq counts from a 10x Genomics platform that need quality-control filtering, normalization, clustering, and marker-gene identification before I can annotate cell types. A couple of collaborators only sent me RDS files from a different single-cell analysis toolkit, which I'll need to convert first.
rows.plain: I have raw single-cell gene-count data from a common droplet-based sequencing platform, and need to filter out low-quality data, normalize it, cluster similar cells, and identify marker genes before labeling cell types. Collaborators also sent RDS-format files from a different single-cell analysis toolkit, which I'll need to convert first.
rows.expert: QC-filter, normalize, cluster, and identify marker genes on raw 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq counts to annotate cell types; also need to convert collaborator-supplied RDS files from another single-cell toolkit first.

rows.synonym: I have a high-dimensional dataset and want to project it down to two dimensions for visualization, preserving both the local neighborhood structure and the broader global structure, ideally with an approach that later lets me embed new points using labels from a subset of my data.
rows.plain: I have a dataset with many variables per point, and want to reduce it to two dimensions for visualization while keeping both close-by relationships and the bigger-picture overall shape intact. Ideally I'd also like a version letting me later add new points into the same layout, guided by labels from part of my existing data.
rows.expert: Project the high-dimensional data to 2D preserving both local and global structure, ideally with a semi-supervised variant supporting later out-of-sample embedding.

rows.synonym: I'm giving a 15-minute conference talk next month covering my recent findings and need to build a visually engaging slide deck with a clear narrative arc, rather than just walls of bulleted text.
rows.plain: Next month I'm giving a short, 15-minute conference talk about my recent research findings. I need a slide presentation that looks visually interesting and tells a clear, connected story from start to finish, instead of slides full of bullet points.
rows.expert: Build a 15-minute conference deck with a clear narrative arc and strong visual design, not bullet-heavy slides.

rows.synonym: I have concentration-time data from a single-dose pharmacokinetic study and need to compute non-compartmental exposure metrics such as AUC and half-life, check whether the terminal elimination phase is well characterized, and then explore whether a two-compartment model provides a better fit.
rows.plain: I have drug-concentration-over-time data from a single-dose study. I need standard exposure measures — total exposure and how long the drug level takes to halve — without assuming a specific compartment model, a check that the late-stage decline is well captured, then a comparison against a two-compartment model.
rows.expert: Compute NCA exposure metrics (AUC, half-life) from single-dose PK data, assess terminal-phase characterization, and evaluate two-compartment model fit.

rows.synonym: Given this raw DNA sequence, can a remotely hosted model identify where the promoter region and the splice donor and acceptor sites are, without my having to download any model weights or use a local GPU?
rows.plain: Using this raw DNA sequence, I want a model running on someone else's server to tell me where the promoter region and the splicing start/stop sites are. I don't want to download any model files myself or need my own graphics card to run it.
rows.expert: Predict promoter and splice donor/acceptor sites from this raw sequence using a hosted model, with no local weight download or GPU required.

rows.synonym: I'm putting together an aggregate evaluation package for a risk-prediction model that our hospital's governance committee is reviewing — a GRADE-style evidence profile, subgroup fairness checks, and calibration documentation — strictly for committee review, not for treating any individual patient.
rows.plain: I'm assembling evidence about a patient-risk-prediction model, for a hospital committee overseeing such tools. This needs a formal evidence-quality summary in the standard medical-evidence grading style, checks for fair performance across patient subgroups, and documentation of how well predicted probabilities match reality — strictly for oversight review, not to guide any patient's treatment.
rows.expert: Prepare an aggregate evaluation package — GRADE-style evidence profile, subgroup fairness checks, calibration documentation — for governance-committee review of a risk-prediction model, not for individual patient care.

rows.synonym: I have a new small-molecule candidate and want to predict its pKa along with a conformer and tautomer ensemble, then dock it against my target protein — all without setting up any local high-performance-computing or GPU infrastructure, just submitting the SMILES string and getting results back.
rows.plain: I have a new candidate drug-like molecule and want predictions of its acid-dissociation behavior, plus a set of possible 3D shapes and alternate chemical forms it could take. Then I want it docked against my target protein to predict binding. I don't want powerful local computing hardware or a graphics card myself — just submit the molecule's text description and get results back.
rows.expert: Predict pKa plus a conformer/tautomer ensemble for the candidate, then dock against the target protein — via SMILES submission only, no local HPC/GPU setup.

rows.synonym: I'm adapting a custom reinforcement-learning simulation environment, built to the standard RL-environment interface, for large-scale training, and need help vectorizing environment rollouts, wiring up a policy-gradient trainer, and safely inspecting a checkpoint file before loading it.
rows.plain: I'm modifying a custom simulated training environment, built to a standard reinforcement-learning interface, for large-scale training. I need help running many copies in parallel, setting up a system that improves the agent's policy directly, and safely checking a saved checkpoint file before loading it.
rows.expert: Adapt a custom reinforcement-learning environment for large-scale training — need vectorized rollouts, a policy-gradient trainer, and safe pre-load inspection of the checkpoint file.

rows.synonym: A colleague shared their draft research-proposal outline and early findings and asked for developmental feedback on the soundness and framing of the idea. I want honest, evidence-traceable comments — not a numeric score or a verdict on fundability.
rows.plain: A colleague shared an early research-proposal outline and preliminary findings, asking for feedback on whether the idea is sound and well-framed. I want honest commentary tied to actual evidence — not a numeric score, and not a final judgment on whether the proposal will get funded.
rows.expert: Give developmental feedback on the soundness and framing of a draft proposal and early findings — evidence-traceable commentary only, no numeric score or fundability verdict.

rows.synonym: I have raw RNA-seq count data from treated versus control samples, with a batch covariate, and need to run differential-expression testing using a multi-factor design, apply log-fold-change shrinkage, and extract genes significant after FDR correction.
rows.plain: I have raw RNA-sequencing gene counts comparing treated versus control samples, processed in different batches I need to account for. I need to test which genes differ significantly while adjusting for batch, apply an adjustment pulling in noisy fold-change estimates, then extract genes significant after correcting for multiple testing.
rows.expert: Run multi-factor differential expression testing (treatment + batch covariate) on raw RNA-seq counts, apply LFC shrinkage, and extract genes significant after FDR correction.

rows.synonym: I have a lengthy piece of writing from a colleague and want to chart their underlying thinking style based on the text alone — how analytical versus intuitive they tend to be, how they balance ethical considerations against strategic ones, and other tensions in how they reason.
rows.plain: A colleague of mine wrote a long document, and just from reading that text, I want to understand their general style of thinking — for example, whether they lean more toward careful analysis or gut instinct, how they balance doing the right thing against doing the strategically smart thing, and any other contrasting tendencies in how they seem to reason.
rows.expert: Infer the author's reasoning-style profile from text alone — analytical-versus-intuitive orientation, ethics-versus-strategy weighting, and other cognitive tensions.

rows.synonym: I want to critically assess the methodology and evidence quality underlying a set of clinical trials — checking for confounders and biases and applying a formal evidence-grading framework — before deciding how much weight to give their conclusions.
rows.plain: I want to carefully examine how well-designed and how trustworthy a group of clinical trials actually are — looking for hidden factors that could distort the results and other sources of bias, and using a formal, standard system for grading the quality of evidence — before I decide how seriously to take what these trials conclude.
rows.expert: Critically appraise trial methodology and evidence quality — confounders, bias, and a formal evidence-grading framework — before weighting the trials' conclusions.

rows.synonym: I need to build a quantum circuit and first run it on a local exact simulator using the standard sampling primitive, then compile it down for an actual IBM quantum processor and execute it through a session with basic error mitigation.
rows.plain: I want to design a quantum circuit and test it on my own computer first, using an exact simulation and the usual measurement-sampling method. Then I want to adapt the circuit for a real IBM quantum computer, run it there through a connected session, using basic techniques to reduce hardware-error effects.
rows.expert: Build a circuit, validate on a local exact simulator with the standard sampler primitive, then transpile for an IBM quantum processor and execute via a session with basic error mitigation.

rows.synonym: I need up-to-date web search results on a fast-moving regulatory topic that changed after your training cutoff, and I'd like to set up a recurring check that flags whenever a specific government webpage changes going forward.
rows.plain: I need to find out the latest information on a regulatory topic that's been changing quickly, likely something that changed after the point where your training data ends. I'd also like to set up something that checks a specific government webpage on a repeating schedule and lets me know whenever it changes.
rows.expert: Need live web-search results on a fast-moving, post-cutoff regulatory topic, plus a recurring change-detection watch on a specific government webpage.

rows.synonym: I have a list of SMILES strings and need to compute molecular descriptors such as molecular weight and TPSA, generate Morgan fingerprints, and run a substructure search using a SMARTS pattern, with fine-grained control over sanitization.
rows.plain: I have a list of molecules written in a standard chemical-structure text notation. I need basic descriptors like molecular weight and polar surface area, a standard type of structural fingerprint, and a search for molecules containing a substructure defined by a pattern-matching notation, with detailed control over cleanup and validation.
rows.expert: Compute molecular descriptors (MW, TPSA) and Morgan fingerprints, and run a SMARTS substructure search, over the SMILES list, with fine-grained sanitization control.

rows.synonym: I want to explore a precision-medicine knowledge graph that integrates more than twenty biomedical databases covering genes, drugs, diseases, and phenotypes, in order to identify which existing drugs might be repurposed for a disease of interest through a shared molecular target.
rows.plain: I want to explore a large connected biomedical information network combining over twenty databases covering genes, drugs, diseases, and observable traits. My goal is finding existing drugs that might be repurposed for a disease I'm interested in, based on sharing a molecular target with drugs already known to work on it.
rows.expert: Query a precision-medicine knowledge graph integrating 20+ biomedical databases (genes, drugs, diseases, phenotypes) to identify drug-repurposing candidates for a target disease via shared molecular targets.

rows.synonym: I've got one flat data table with several hundred million records — too large to fit in my system's working memory — and I need to calculate quick summary statistics and build a 2D density heatmap from it, without ever pulling the full table into memory at once.
rows.plain: I have one big spreadsheet-like file with hundreds of millions of rows, and it's too large to fit in my computer's working memory all at once. I need to quickly calculate summary numbers (like counts, averages, totals) across it, and also produce a picture that shows where data points cluster densely versus sparsely, all without loading the entire file into memory in one go.
rows.expert: Need out-of-core aggregation and 2D density-heatmap construction over a >100M-row tabular dataset that exceeds available RAM, processed without full in-memory materialization.

rows.synonym: I'm writing the opening section of a paper about impaired mitochondrial function in Parkinson's disease, and I need a well-verified collection of recent references spanning the rival mechanistic theories, so every statement I make can be traced to a genuine source.
rows.plain: I'm writing the opening part of a research paper about how the energy-producing structures inside nerve cells break down in a common movement disorder involving tremor and stiffness. I need a solid set of recent, double-checked references that cover the different competing explanations for why this happens, so that every statement I make in the paper can be linked back to a real, verifiable published source.
rows.expert: Drafting the introduction on mitochondrial dysfunction in PD; need a curated, verified bibliography spanning competing mechanistic hypotheses with full traceability per claim.

rows.synonym: I have a batch of untargeted metabolomics tandem mass spectrometry spectra saved in a common open spectral text format, and I need to clean the data, standardize the precursor mass and adduct annotations, and compare each spectrum against a reference spectral collection using cosine-similarity scoring to identify matches.
rows.plain: I have a collection of chemical fingerprint measurements taken with an instrument that breaks molecules apart and records the fragment masses, saved in a common shareable text file. I need to clean up this data, make the molecule-charge and parent-mass labels consistent across all the entries, and then compare each measurement against a library of known reference fingerprints, scoring how similar they are, to find which known compounds they likely match.
rows.expert: Need MGF-format untargeted MS/MS preprocessing with precursor/adduct metadata harmonization, then cosine-similarity spectral library matching against a reference database.

rows.synonym: For one clearly specified inherited variant, identified by its standard reference SNP number, I need to retrieve gene-disease validity claims along with citation-linked supporting publications; if the identifier turns out to be ambiguous, the lookup should halt cleanly and report that, rather than guessing at which variant was intended.
rows.plain: I have one specific inherited genetic change, identified by its standard reference number, and I want to find out what's been established about whether the gene it sits in is truly linked to a disease, plus the published studies that back up that link, with sources attached. If that reference number could actually point to more than one variant, I want the process to stop and tell me clearly, instead of just picking one and guessing.
rows.expert: For a single rsID-identified germline variant, retrieve gene-disease validity classifications with source-linked literature; require a hard stop with an ambiguity flag on non-unique rsID resolution rather than heuristic disambiguation.

rows.synonym: I have scanned document pages in a fixed-layout format that need text recognition, and for every recognized word I need its precise bounding-box position on the page, along with an image render of each page so a vision-capable AI system can look at them — all done on my own machine, with no calls to any remote service.
rows.plain: I have pictures of scanned pages that need to have their text automatically read and recognized. For each word that gets recognized, I need to know exactly where it sits on the page, given as box coordinates. I also need a plain picture-file version of each page, so that an AI system that can look at images (not just read text) can inspect them. All of this needs to run entirely on my own computer, without sending anything to an outside internet service.
rows.expert: Need local (no external API) OCR over scanned PDF pages with per-word bounding-box coordinates, plus per-page PNG rasterization for downstream multimodal-agent inspection.

rows.synonym: I have a text dataset with labels, and I want to run a repeating, language-model-assisted procedure that generates and rates candidate wording patterns as hypotheses, then improves the collection of patterns using information drawn from published literature.
rows.plain: I have a collection of text examples that are each tagged with a category, and I want a repeated back-and-forth process, guided by a language-generating AI, that comes up with possible word or phrase patterns as guesses for what distinguishes the categories, scores how good each guess is, and then improves that set of guesses using facts pulled from published research articles.
rows.expert: Need an iterative LLM-in-the-loop pipeline over a labeled text corpus that proposes and scores candidate lexical/pattern hypotheses, then refines the hypothesis bank using literature-derived evidence.

rows.synonym: I already have a fitted model and want to understand why it produced particular outputs for a handful of unseen test cases, using rigorous credit-assignment values that I can verify actually sum to the model's true output, rather than an informal guess at which inputs mattered.
rows.plain: I have a model I already built and trained, and for a few examples it hasn't seen before, I want to understand why it gave the specific answers it did. I want a mathematically sound way of assigning credit to each input feature, one where I can check that the credited amounts genuinely add up to match the model's actual output — not just an informal guess about which inputs seemed important.
rows.expert: Need post-hoc, additive feature-attribution explanations (e.g. Shapley-consistent) for a trained model's predictions on specific held-out instances, with verifiable efficiency (attributions sum to the model output).

rows.synonym: I have a dataset organized in rows and columns and want to construct and cross-validate a handful of traditional classification algorithms, optimize their hyperparameters through an exhaustive grid search, and evaluate them side by side within a tidy preprocessing workflow before settling on a final model.
rows.plain: I have a dataset arranged as a table and want to build a few standard, well-established prediction methods that sort items into categories, test each one carefully using repeated data splits, and systematically try out different setting combinations to find the best ones. I want to do all of this inside one clean, organized sequence of data-preparation and modeling steps, comparing the methods fairly, before choosing which one to use as my final answer.
rows.expert: Need cross-validated benchmarking of several classical classifiers with grid-search hyperparameter tuning inside a unified preprocessing pipeline, for final model selection.

rows.synonym: I want to train a graph-based neural network to forecast toxicity and other pharmacokinetic and safety properties for drug-like compounds, and benchmark its performance against established, publicly published molecular datasets and their standard train/test splits.
rows.plain: I want to train a machine-learning model that represents each drug-like molecule as a network of connected atoms, and use it to predict how toxic or otherwise pharmacologically risky the molecule might be, along with related absorption and metabolism properties. I want to test its performance against well-known, publicly available collections of molecules and the standard way those collections are divided for fair comparison.
rows.expert: Need to train a GNN for ADMET/toxicity prediction on drug-like molecules, benchmarked against standard published molecular datasets and their canonical splits.

rows.synonym: I have a spreadsheet-style file of text-based chemical structure codes that I need to standardize into a single canonical form, calculate molecular descriptors and fingerprints for, and then group into a diverse, representative subset — all with as little repetitive setup code as possible.
rows.plain: I have a plain text-table file listing molecules, each written as a short text code describing its chemical structure. I need to put these codes into one consistent standard form, calculate a set of numerical properties and structural fingerprints for each molecule, and then group similar molecules together so I can pick out a smaller, varied set that still represents the whole collection well. I want to do this with very little extra setup code.
rows.expert: Need SMILES standardization/canonicalization, descriptor and fingerprint computation, and diversity-based clustering into a representative subset, with minimal boilerplate.

rows.synonym: I have an engineering design challenge with several objectives and restrictions that pull against each other, and I want to identify the Pareto-optimal trade-off solutions with a multi-objective evolutionary search method, then plot the resulting front for a presentation.
rows.plain: I have an engineering design problem where I'm trying to satisfy several goals at once, and improving one goal often makes another one worse, all while staying within certain limits. I want to use a search method inspired by natural selection, which tries out and evolves many candidate designs, to find the best set of trade-off solutions — ones where you can't improve one goal without harming another. Then I want to draw a chart of those trade-off solutions to show in a presentation.
rows.expert: Need multi-objective evolutionary optimization to identify the Pareto front for a constrained engineering design problem, plus a presentation-ready plot of the front.

rows.synonym: I have time-to-event data, including patients lost to follow-up, for a group of patients, and I want to fit a proportional-hazards regression model together with a random survival forest, then assess both using a concordance measure and a time-dependent prediction-error metric, handling the incomplete follow-up correctly throughout.
rows.plain: I have data tracking how long each patient was followed and whether or when something happened to them, noting that some patients dropped out of monitoring before anything happened. I want to fit two different models that predict how survival time relates to patient characteristics — one a standard statistical regression approach, the other a machine-learning approach based on many decision trees — and then judge how good each one is at ranking and predicting outcomes over time, making sure the patients who dropped out early are accounted for properly rather than treated as if nothing happened to them.
rows.expert: Need to fit a Cox PH model and a random survival forest on right-censored cohort follow-up data, then evaluate both via concordance and time-dependent Brier score, with proper censoring handling.

rows.synonym: I want to construct a multilevel Bayesian model for my nested experimental data, sample the posterior using a No-U-Turn Hamiltonian MCMC sampler, examine convergence diagnostics, and compare it against a simpler alternative model using leave-one-out cross-validation.
rows.plain: I have experimental data with a nested, multi-level structure (for example, measurements grouped within subjects grouped within sites), and I want to build a probability-based model that accounts for that structure. I want to fit it using a modern sampling method that explores the space of possible parameter values efficiently, check that the fitting process actually settled on stable answers, and then compare this model against a simpler one by seeing how well each predicts data it wasn't fitted on, one point at a time.
rows.expert: Need a hierarchical Bayesian model for multilevel data fit via NUTS-HMC, with convergence diagnostics, then LOO-CV model comparison against a simpler baseline.

rows.synonym: I need to retrieve the currently published version of a lab protocol from our protocols.io project, verify its DOI and its history of prior versions, and preview how a suggested edit to one step would look before I actually commit any change.
rows.plain: I need to fetch the latest officially published version of one of our lab's written procedures from our shared protocols.io project, double-check its permanent citation identifier and see the record of earlier versions, and then look at a preview of how a proposed change to one step would appear, without actually applying that change yet.
rows.expert: Need to fetch the current published protocol version and DOI/version history from our protocols.io project, and preview a proposed step edit as a diff before committing it.

rows.synonym: I'm uncertain about which strategic path to take for my lab, and I'd like several genuinely opposing expert perspectives — one focused on systems-level thinking, one pragmatic, one ethical — to be argued against each other in a structured debate before I make my decision.
rows.plain: I can't decide on the right strategic direction for my lab, and I want to hear several different expert points of view that genuinely disagree with each other — someone who thinks about how all the parts of a system interact, someone focused on what's practically doable, and someone focused on what's right or fair — argued against one another in an organized way, before I make my final choice.
rows.expert: Need a structured multi-perspective debate (systems, pragmatist, ethicist viewpoints) on lab strategic direction prior to decision.

rows.synonym: I need to retrieve one particular gene's entries across multiple public reference-ID systems by calling each database's own documented interface, keeping a complete record of which endpoints, filters, and pagination settings were used, rather than recalling the answer from memorized knowledge.
rows.plain: I need to look up one specific gene's information across several different public reference-numbering systems, going directly through each database's own official access method rather than relying on remembered facts, and I want a full written trail showing exactly which web addresses, search filters, and page-by-page settings were used to get each piece of information.
rows.expert: Need live, API-driven cross-referencing of a gene across multiple public identifier systems with full endpoint/filter/pagination provenance, no memorized lookups.

rows.synonym: I just want a fast lookup of the predicted protein structure and basic gene details for a couple of genes from the AlphaFold structure database — nothing fancy, no large automated workflow.
rows.plain: I just want a quick check of the computationally predicted 3D shape of the protein and some basic background information for a couple of genes — nothing elaborate, and definitely no big automated multi-step process.
rows.expert: Need a quick AlphaFold structure and basic gene-info lookup for a couple of genes — no pipeline needed.

rows.synonym: My array-processing and tabular-join preprocessing workflow for a large dataset runs too slowly on the processor, and I want to shift the array computations and table-merging operations onto our graphics accelerator, without altering the numerical results.
rows.plain: The step-by-step process I use to clean and prepare a large dataset — involving numerical array math and combining tables together — is too slow when it runs on my computer's main processor. I want to move that same math and those same table-combining steps onto our graphics-card hardware instead, so it runs faster, while making sure the actual numbers that come out stay exactly the same.
rows.expert: Need to port a CPU-bound array/dataframe-join preprocessing pipeline to GPU execution with numerically identical results.

rows.synonym: I need to retrieve a batch of DNA construct entries from our Benchling registry and update the corresponding electronic lab notebook entries for a new set of samples, using the API.
rows.plain: I need to fetch a group of DNA-design records stored in our Benchling registry, and then use its programmatic interface to update the matching digital lab-notebook entries for a new batch of samples.
rows.expert: Need to batch-pull DNA construct records from our Benchling registry and update matching ELN entries for new samples via the API.

rows.synonym: I want to explore what's documented about an indirect, two-step connection between a particular gene and a disease within a structured biomedical knowledge graph, along with the supporting publications and origin-source details for each connecting link.
rows.plain: I want to find out what's known about an indirect link — one that goes through an intermediate step — between a specific gene and a disease, using a structured network of biomedical facts and relationships. For each connecting link in that chain, I want to see the published research that supports it and where that information originally came from.
rows.expert: Need two-hop gene-disease path traversal over a structured biomedical knowledge graph, with per-edge supporting literature and data-source provenance.

rows.synonym: I want to obtain a copy of a large public brain-imaging dataset without fetching every single file immediately, and I need to log precisely how each analysis output is produced so that a collaborator can later re-run my entire workflow from scratch.
