rows.plain: I want to get a working local copy of a big publicly shared set of brain-scan data, but without having to download every single file right away — just what's needed as I go. I also need to keep a precise, complete record of exactly how each result was produced, so that someone else on my team can later repeat my whole analysis from start to finish and get the same results.
rows.expert: Need lazy/on-demand cloning of a large public neuroimaging dataset plus full provenance capture for downstream pipeline re-execution by a collaborator.

rows.synonym: I need to conduct a systematic search of the biomedical literature database, the physics/math preprint archive, and other scholarly repositories on a research topic, organize the findings into themed sections, check every citation for accuracy, and generate a properly formatted document suitable for the background section of a manuscript.
rows.plain: I need to thoroughly search several major research-paper repositories — including the main biomedical-literature database and a popular preprint archive — on a given research topic, then organize what I find into themed sections, double-check that every reference is accurate and real, and put together a properly formatted write-up that I can use as the background section of a paper.
rows.expert: Need a systematic PubMed/arXiv (plus other databases) literature search on a topic, synthesized into thematic sections with citation verification, formatted for a manuscript background section.

rows.synonym: I want to gather gene expression measurements and cell-type labels for a given tissue and disease across numerous public single-cell studies simultaneously, without fetching each underlying dataset one by one, in order to assemble a large reference set spanning multiple studies.
rows.plain: I want to pull together gene activity readings and cell-type labels for a specific body tissue and disease, drawing from many different publicly available single-cell studies all at once, without having to separately download each individual study's data. The goal is to build one large combined reference collection spanning many studies.
rows.expert: Need cross-study aggregation of expression values and cell-type metadata for a tissue/disease from multiple public single-cell datasets via a unified query, without per-dataset downloads, to build a large reference atlas.

rows.synonym: I have whole-slide hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained pathology images that I need to load and cut into smaller patches, pass through a quality-control workflow, and use to construct spatial graphs from multiplex-stained cells — all running on my own machine, strictly for exploratory research and not for diagnostic use.
rows.plain: I have very large, full-slide microscope images of tissue stained with a standard two-color pathology stain, and I need to load them and cut them into smaller square pieces, run them through a set of quality checks, and use cell positions from separately multi-color-stained images to build maps of which cells sit near which other cells. This all needs to run entirely on my own computer, and it's strictly for exploratory research, not for making any diagnosis.
rows.expert: Need local WSI H&E loading/tiling into patches, a QC pipeline, and spatial-graph construction from multiplex-stained cell data, for exploratory research use only.

rows.synonym: I want to predict the three-dimensional structure of a protein bound to a small molecule, and screen a batch of candidate binding compounds through docking calculations, all running on managed cloud graphics-processing resources, since I'd rather not set up or maintain my own local GPU hardware for these structure-prediction jobs.
rows.plain: I want to predict what the 3D shape looks like when a protein and a small candidate drug molecule bind together, and then test a whole batch of possible binding molecules by simulating how well each one might dock into the protein. I want all of this computing to happen on graphics-processing hardware that's rented and managed in the cloud, because I don't want to buy, set up, or maintain that kind of hardware myself.
rows.expert: Need protein-ligand complex structure prediction and batch docking screens executed on managed cloud GPU infrastructure, with no local GPU provisioning.

rows.synonym: I have a batch of newly designed protein sequences that I want to submit through a remote lab's automated experiment interface to run binding, thermal-stability, and expression assays, then retrieve the results once those runs are complete.
rows.plain: I have a set of newly designed protein sequences, and I want to send them, through a programmatic interface, to a remote laboratory service that will physically run experiments testing how well each protein binds its target, how stable it is under heat, and how well it's produced by cells. Once those experiments finish, I want to collect the results back.
rows.expert: Need to submit designed protein sequences via a remote/cloud lab's experiment API for binding, thermostability, and expression assays, then retrieve completed run results.

rows.synonym: I want to search complete biomedical research articles together with FDA and EMA regulatory submission documents and clinical-trial protocols, all within one unified, plain-text-searchable archive, with citations anchored to exact line numbers for verification; I've already got an access key set up for this.
rows.plain: I want to search the full text of biomedical research papers together with official drug-regulator filings (from both the US and European regulators) and clinical-trial protocol documents, all in one combined archive that lets me search through plain text directly, with each citation pointing to the exact line it came from so I can double-check it. I already have the access credentials set up for this.
rows.expert: Need unified full-text search across biomedical literature, FDA/EMA regulatory filings, and clinical-trial protocols in a plain-text-indexed archive with line-level citation provenance; API key already configured.

rows.synonym: I want to set up a self-hosted, privacy-respecting substitute for a well-known cloud note-and-document assistant, where I can upload PDFs and recorded talks, converse with them in context, and generate a multi-speaker audio podcast summarizing my research notes.
rows.plain: I want to set up my own privately hosted version of a well-known online tool that lets you upload documents and audio recordings, ask it questions about their content in context, and have it produce an audio conversation between multiple simulated speakers summarizing your notes — but running entirely under my own control, without sending anything to an outside company.
rows.expert: Need a self-hosted, privacy-preserving analog to a well-known document-chat assistant: PDF/talk-recording ingestion, contextual chat, and multi-speaker podcast-style summary generation.

rows.synonym: My lab has just finished a major experiment, and I want the team to independently come up with and openly evaluate several possible follow-up research directions, documenting our assumptions and points of disagreement before we settle on one path.
rows.plain: My lab just finished a big experiment, and now I want each team member to independently think up several possible next research directions, and then openly compare and evaluate them together as a group. I want to make sure we write down what assumptions each idea relies on and where we disagree with each other, before we commit to just one direction.
rows.expert: Need independent generation and transparent team evaluation of candidate follow-up research directions post-experiment, with captured assumptions and disagreements prior to path commitment.

rows.synonym: I need to construct a fully custom chart featuring a broken axis, an inset magnified panel, and a bespoke color scale, since the higher-level charting shortcuts don't give me fine enough control over every element, and then export the result as a scalable vector PDF.
rows.plain: I need to build a highly customized chart that has a gap in one of its axes, a small zoomed-in inset view, and a custom set of colors, because the simpler, ready-made charting options don't let me control every visual detail precisely enough. Once it's built, I need to save it as a scalable, print-quality document rather than a fixed-resolution picture.
rows.expert: Need low-level, element-by-element chart construction (broken axis, inset zoom panel, custom colormap) beyond high-level plotting APIs, exported as a vector PDF.

rows.synonym: Before committing resources to a single direction, I want to sketch out several branching what-if scenarios for my research program in case a critical reagent supplier suddenly fails to deliver — a best case, a worst case, a most-likely case, and a couple of wildcard outcomes — each with rough probability estimates and consequences.
rows.plain: Before I decide how to commit resources, I want to think through several different possible future paths for my research program, in case an important supplier of a key material suddenly can't provide it anymore. I want a best-case outcome, a worst-case outcome, the most likely outcome, and a couple of unlikely-but-possible surprise outcomes, each with a rough estimate of how likely it is and what would follow from it.
rows.expert: Need a branching scenario analysis (best/worst/likely/wildcard) for research-program continuity risk under key reagent-supply disruption, with rough probabilities and consequences, prior to resource commitment.

rows.synonym: I have variant call files from an ongoing population-genomics cohort study, and I need to load them into a searchable data store that lets me incorporate new samples incrementally, without having to re-merge the entire collection each time, and then efficiently retrieve variant calls for particular genomic regions across thousands of samples.
rows.plain: I have genetic-variant result files coming from an ongoing large study of many people's genomes, and I need to load them into a system I can search, where I can add new people's data over time without having to redo the whole combination process from scratch each time. I also need to be able to quickly pull out the genetic variants found in specific stretches of the genome, across thousands of people, without it being slow.
rows.expert: Need incrementally updatable, queryable VCF ingestion for an ongoing population cohort, with efficient region-based variant retrieval across thousands of samples without full re-merge.

rows.synonym: I need to know which SARS-CoV-2 Pango lineages are currently spreading and expanding the quickest, and whether a particular lineage designation I encountered in an older report has since been retired or given a new name.
rows.plain: I want to know which strains of the pandemic coronavirus are currently spreading and increasing in frequency the fastest, using the standard naming system for viral lineages. I also want to check whether one specific strain name I saw in an older report has since been discontinued or replaced with a different name.
rows.expert: Need current fastest-growing SARS-CoV-2 Pango lineages, and a withdrawal/rename check for a specific historical lineage designation.

rows.synonym: I want to run many cycles of automated trials to improve my automated-agent framework's accuracy on a benchmark, structuring each trial as a branch stemming from a shared hypothesis so that findings build cumulatively, and using a held-out test split that's never used during search, to keep from overfitting to the metric I'm optimizing.
rows.plain: I want to run many repeated rounds of automated testing to make my automated testing framework more accurate on a standard benchmark, where each individual trial branches off from a shared underlying idea, so that what's learned in one trial carries over and builds on the last. I also want to keep a separate portion of the test data completely untouched during all this searching, and only use it at the very end to check results, so I don't just end up tricking myself into a good-looking score without a real improvement.
rows.expert: Need iterative, hypothesis-branched automated experimentation to improve agent-harness benchmark accuracy, with a strictly held-out eval split excluded from search to prevent metric overfitting.

rows.synonym: I have a folder of local medical-imaging files, in the standard clinical imaging format, from a study I'm authorized to use for research, and I need to examine and safely remove patient-identifying metadata fields before exporting the raw pixel data for a de-identified pilot dataset.
rows.plain: I have a folder of medical scan files, saved in the standard hospital imaging format, from a study I have permission to use for research. I need to look through the hidden information attached to each file and safely remove anything that could identify the patient, before pulling out just the raw image data to build a de-identified sample dataset.
rows.expert: Need local DICOM metadata inspection and safe de-identification (stripping patient-identifying tags) prior to pixel-array export for a de-identified pilot dataset.

rows.synonym: I have taxonomic abundance tables produced by a 16S ribosomal or shotgun metagenomic sequencing workflow, and I want to convert each microbiome sample into a fixed-length embedding using a pretrained microbiome foundation model, cluster the samples by similarity, and later fine-tune that same model to predict a phenotype from community composition.
rows.plain: I have tables showing how much of each type of microbe is present in different microbiome samples, generated using one of two standard community-profiling sequencing approaches. I want to turn each sample into a fixed-length list of numbers using an already-trained general-purpose microbiome model, group the samples by how similar those numbers are, and later further train that same model to predict a specific trait or outcome based on which microbes are present.
rows.expert: Need to embed 16S/shotgun-metagenomics taxonomic abundance profiles via a pretrained microbiome foundation model into fixed-size vectors for clustering, with downstream fine-tuning for phenotype prediction from community composition.

rows.synonym: I need to compute pairwise overlaps and consensus coverage across a set of genomic interval files, and also tokenize those regions for a downstream machine-learning model, with everything running entirely on my own machine and no network access.
rows.plain: I need to figure out where multiple sets of genome location ranges overlap with each other and how much of the genome they agree on covering, and I also need to convert those location ranges into a token format usable by a downstream machine-learning model. All of this has to run entirely on my own computer, with no internet connections made at all.
rows.expert: Need pairwise interval-overlap and consensus-coverage computation across multiple genomic interval files, plus region tokenization for a downstream ML model — fully local, no network calls.

rows.synonym: I have crystal-structure files produced by density-functional-theory calculations, and I want to check their symmetry, construct a phase diagram from the computed formation energies, and query the Materials Project database for comparable entries.
rows.plain: I have files describing the atomic structure of crystals, generated using a standard quantum-mechanical calculation method. I want to check the symmetry of these structures, build a diagram showing which combinations are stable based on their calculated formation energy, and look up the Materials Project database for similar known entries.
rows.expert: Need symmetry analysis of DFT-derived crystal structures, phase-diagram construction from computed formation energies, and cross-referencing against the Materials Project database.

rows.synonym: I already have separate mature and nascent transcript count layers for my single-cell dataset, produced by a splicing-aware alignment tool, and I want to infer the directionality of cell differentiation and identify the genes driving that transition, building on the embedding I've already generated in my regular single-cell analysis toolkit.
rows.plain: I already have two related sets of gene-count measurements for my single-cell data — one for the fully processed transcripts and one for the newly made, unprocessed ones — produced by a sequencing-alignment tool that's aware of gene splicing. I want to figure out which direction cells are moving as they change and mature over time, and identify which genes are driving that change, using the reduced-dimension map of my cells that I've already built with my usual single-cell analysis tools.
rows.expert: Need RNA-velocity inference (differentiation direction) and driver-gene identification from spliced/unspliced count layers, layered onto an existing single-cell embedding.

rows.synonym: I have an astronomical image in the standard flexible image transport format with world-coordinate-system header keywords, and I need to convert pixel positions into sky coordinates expressed in a different reference frame, as well as compute the luminosity distance of an object at a specified redshift.
rows.plain: I have a standard astronomy image file that has embedded information linking pixel positions to real sky positions. I need to convert specific pixel locations in the image into celestial coordinates, but expressed using a different reference system than the one built into the file, and I also need to calculate how far away, in a specific cosmological distance measure, an object is given how much its light has been stretched by the universe's expansion.
rows.expert: Need WCS-based pixel-to-sky coordinate transformation (into a different reference frame) from a FITS header, plus luminosity-distance computation at a given redshift.

rows.synonym: I want to build a discrete-event simulation modeling patients arriving at a clinic, waiting in line for a limited number of exam rooms, and being attended to by staff whose service durations are random, then compare average waiting times across different staffing levels using multiple simulation replications.
rows.plain: I want to build a computer simulation that models patients showing up at a clinic over time, waiting in a queue because there are only a limited number of exam rooms, and then being seen by staff whose time spent with each patient varies randomly. I want to try this simulation with a few different numbers of staff on duty and compare the average waiting times, running each staffing scenario multiple times to make sure the comparison is reliable.
rows.expert: Need a discrete-event simulation of clinic patient arrivals with resource-constrained (exam-room) queueing and stochastic service times, comparing mean wait times across staffing levels over multiple replications.

rows.synonym: I'm setting up a turbulence simulation using a periodic pseudospectral numerical method, and I need help choosing the solver, checking my grid resolution, time step, and Courant number against my available compute budget, and validating a small-scale pilot run before scaling up to a multi-node job.
rows.plain: I'm setting up a fluid-turbulence simulation that uses a mathematical method based on repeating wave patterns across a periodic domain, and I need help picking the right numerical solving approach, and checking that my grid detail level, the size of my time steps, and a key stability number are all sensible given how much computing power I have available. I also want to run a tiny test version first and check that it behaves correctly before I scale the whole thing up to run across many computers at once.
rows.expert: Need solver selection and resolution/time-step/CFL validation against compute budget for a periodic pseudospectral turbulence simulation, plus a small-scale pilot run before multi-node scale-up.

rows.synonym: I have matched tumor and normal long-read sequencing alignment files with their accompanying index files, and I need to construct a compliant sample sheet, produce the necessary launch files, run a dry-run validation check, and then submit the job to our high-performance computing job-scheduling cluster.
rows.plain: I have paired cancer-tumor and normal-tissue sequencing files from a long-read sequencing technology, along with their matching index files. I need to put together a properly formatted sample list, generate the files needed to start the analysis job, run a test check to make sure everything's set up correctly without actually running it yet, and then send the real job off to run on our shared computing cluster.
rows.expert: Need to build a compliant samplesheet and launch artifacts from matched tumor-normal PacBio BAM/pbi files, run dry-run validation, then submit to our HPC job-scheduling cluster.

rows.synonym: Our imaging facility operates an OMERO server, and I need a script that authenticates to it, retrieves region-of-interest annotations and metadata for a batch of microscopy images, and exports them to local storage.
rows.plain: Our imaging facility runs a shared server, called OMERO, that stores microscopy images, and I need a script that logs into it, pulls out the marked regions of interest and other descriptive information for a batch of images, and saves them onto my own computer.
rows.expert: Need a script to authenticate against our OMERO server and batch-export ROI annotations and metadata for a set of microscopy images locally.

rows.synonym: I have raw paired-end sequencing reads from a bulk transcriptome experiment comparing a treated group against a control, and I want to go from quality control and read alignment all the way through to a list of differentially expressed genes and enriched biological pathways, within a single reproducible workflow.
rows.plain: I have raw paired sequencing read data from an experiment measuring overall gene activity in samples, comparing a treated group to an untreated control group. I want a single, reproducible, step-by-step process that starts with checking read quality and aligning the reads to the genome, and ends with a list of genes whose activity differs between groups, plus the biological pathways that are over-represented among those genes.
rows.expert: Need an end-to-end reproducible bulk RNA-seq pipeline: QC, alignment, differential expression, and pathway enrichment, for a treatment-vs-control paired-end design.

rows.synonym: I want to determine whether a particular gene is selectively required for survival in cancer cell lines carrying KRAS mutations, using dependency scores from genome-wide CRISPR knockout screens, in order to assess it as a potential drug target.
rows.plain: I want to check whether a specific gene is especially important for the survival of cancer cells that carry a particular cancer-driving mutation, compared to cells without that mutation, using data from large-scale gene-editing screens that measure how much each cell line depends on each gene. The goal is to judge whether this gene could be a good target for a new drug.
rows.expert: Need to assess selective essentiality of a gene in KRAS-mutant lines using genome-wide CRISPR knockout dependency scores, for drug-target evaluation.

rows.synonym: I want to check my project's literature-recommendation feed for new entries, open one to read the note explaining why it's relevant, and export the definitive version of the paper as a plain-text markup document so I can read it offline.
rows.plain: I want to check whether there's anything new in the feed that suggests research papers relevant to my project, open one of the suggestions to read the short note explaining why it was flagged as relevant, and then save the official version of that paper as a simple, readable text file, so I can read it later without an internet connection.
rows.expert: Need to check the project's paper-recommendation feed, review a relevance note, and export the canonical paper as markdown for offline reading.

rows.synonym: I have a genome-scale metabolic model saved in the standard systems-biology model-exchange format, and I want to run flux-balance analysis together with a gene-knockout screen to identify which gene deletions are lethal or growth-limiting under a specified growth medium.
rows.plain: I have a computer model representing all the metabolic reactions encoded across an organism's whole genome, saved in the standard file format used for sharing these kinds of biological models. I want to simulate how nutrients flow through the network to predict growth rate, and then test, one gene at a time, which gene removals would kill the organism or severely limit its growth under a specific set of nutrient conditions.
rows.expert: Need FBA plus a systematic gene-knockout screen on an SBML genome-scale metabolic reconstruction, under a defined growth medium, to identify lethal/growth-limiting genes.

rows.synonym: I have a single-cell gene-expression matrix and want to infer which transcription factors control which target genes, using a scalable, tree-based ensemble method that can be distributed in parallel across multiple processor cores.
rows.plain: I have a table of gene-activity measurements from individual cells, and I want to figure out which master regulator genes are controlling which other genes, using a machine-learning approach based on many decision trees that can run in parallel to handle a large number of processing cores efficiently.
rows.expert: Need gene regulatory network inference (TF-to-target) from a single-cell expression matrix using a scalable, tree-ensemble-based method, parallelized across cores.

rows.synonym: I'm conducting an evidence synthesis and need organized, study-by-study experimental details — methodology, sample sizes, and quality ratings — extracted from the full text of studies on a given topic, not merely their titles and abstracts.
rows.plain: I'm pulling together and summarizing evidence across many research studies on a topic, and for each individual study I need organized details about how the experiment was run, how many subjects were included, and how good the study quality was — and I need this pulled from the complete text of each paper, not just from the short summary or title.
rows.expert: Need structured, per-study data extraction (methods, sample size, quality score) from full-text articles for an evidence synthesis, not abstract-level only.

rows.synonym: I have a single daily sales time series and want a fast, no-training forecast complete with well-calibrated prediction intervals, without having to train or fine-tune any custom model myself.
rows.plain: I have one simple series of daily sales numbers over time, and I want a quick prediction of future values, including a reliable range of uncertainty around each prediction, without having to build, train, or adjust any custom forecasting model myself.
rows.expert: Need a zero-shot univariate forecast with calibrated prediction intervals for a daily sales series, no custom model training/fine-tuning.

rows.synonym: I have a directory of sequence files in the standard FASTA and GenBank formats that I need to parse programmatically, run through automated similarity searches against NCBI's sequence databases, and integrate into a custom batch-processing workflow.
rows.plain: I have a folder of gene and protein sequence files saved in two standard bioinformatics text formats, and I need to read them into code automatically, run automated searches comparing them against public sequence databases run by the US national biotechnology information center, and combine all of that into my own custom, repeatable batch-processing workflow.
rows.expert: Need programmatic parsing of FASTA/GenBank files, automated NCBI similarity searches, and integration into a custom batch pipeline.

rows.synonym: I have an in-memory tabular dataset from an experiment and want to rapidly assemble box plots, violin plots, and a correlation heatmap to explore differences between groups, before deciding what deserves refinement into a polished final figure.
rows.plain: I have a table of experimental results already loaded into my analysis environment, and I just want to quickly throw together some simple comparison charts — box-and-whisker plots, violin-shaped distribution plots, and a color-coded grid showing how strongly variables relate to each other — to explore differences between groups, before deciding which of these is worth turning into a polished, final figure.
rows.expert: Need quick exploratory box plots, violin plots, and a correlation heatmap from an in-memory tabular dataset, for group-difference exploration prior to final-figure polishing.

rows.synonym: I need to open a sorted, indexed sequence-alignment file, retrieve all reads that overlap a particular genomic region, exclude secondary and supplementary alignments, and calculate per-base sequencing depth, including positions with zero coverage.
rows.plain: I need to open a sorted and indexed file of aligned sequencing reads, pull out every read that overlaps a specific stretch of the genome, remove any reads that are secondary or supplementary duplicate alignments, and then calculate how many reads cover each individual genomic position, making sure to include positions that have no coverage at all rather than skipping them.
rows.expert: Need to query a sorted/indexed BAM for reads overlapping a region, exclude secondary/supplementary alignments, and compute per-base depth including zero-coverage positions.

rows.synonym: I have a list of noncoding single-nucleotide variants from a fine-mapped genome-wide association credible set, mapped to the standard human reference genome, and I want to rank which ones most likely disrupt regulatory function — enhancers, promoters, splicing, or chromatin accessibility — using precomputed genome-wide effect scores and their underlying feature-level contributions.
rows.plain: I have a shortlist of single-letter genetic variants, sitting outside of protein-coding regions, that came from narrowing down a genome-wide association study to its most likely causal candidates, all positioned according to the standard human genome map. I want to figure out which of these variants are most likely to disrupt gene-control activity — things like on-switches, promoters, splicing signals, or how open or closed the DNA packaging is — using scores that were already computed genome-wide to measure this kind of effect, along with a breakdown of which underlying features drove each score.
rows.expert: Need to prioritize noncoding SNVs from a fine-mapped GWAS credible set (GRCh-build coordinates) for regulatory disruption (enhancer/promoter/splicing/chromatin accessibility) using precomputed genome-wide variant-effect scores and their feature attributions.

rows.synonym: I have unaligned, evolutionarily related protein sequences from multiple species, and I want to align them, construct a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree with automated model selection, and then visualize and annotate the resulting tree.
rows.plain: I have protein sequences from several different species that are related by common ancestry but haven't yet been lined up against each other. I want to line them up, then build a best-fit evolutionary tree using a statistical approach that also automatically picks the most suitable underlying model, and finally draw and label that tree nicely.
rows.expert: Need multiple sequence alignment of homologous proteins across species, ML tree inference with model selection, and tree visualization/annotation.

rows.synonym: I have raw wideband recordings from a high-density silicon electrode probe that I need to preprocess, correct for probe drift over the recording, run through spike-sorting to identify individual neurons, and then compute quality metrics to curate the resulting units.
rows.plain: I have raw electrical recordings taken from a densely packed silicon recording probe with many closely spaced electrode contacts, and I need to clean up the signal, correct for the probe having physically shifted position slightly during recording, separate the recorded signals into activity from individual neurons, and then calculate quality scores to decide which of those identified neurons are trustworthy enough to keep.
rows.expert: Need preprocessing and drift correction for raw high-density silicon-probe recordings, spike sorting, and unit quality-metric computation for curation.

rows.synonym: I need to compute overlap and nearest-feature operations between two large genomic interval files in the standard BED format, and separately read per-position coverage depth directly from a sequence-alignment file, all without loading the full files into memory, ideally streaming directly from cloud object storage.
rows.plain: I need to figure out where the regions in two large genome-location files overlap and which is the closest feature to each region, and separately read, position by position, how much sequencing coverage there is directly from an alignment file — all without loading the entire files into memory at once, and ideally reading straight from cloud-based storage rather than downloading first.
rows.expert: Need overlap/nearest-feature operations between two large BED files and streaming per-position depth extraction from a BAM, without full in-memory loading, ideally reading directly from cloud object storage.

rows.synonym: I need to search the internet for recent technical write-ups on a particular method, and also retrieve and extract the full text from several specific article web addresses and academic PDF documents, all in a single batch.
rows.plain: I need to search online for recent, detailed explanations of a specific technical method, and also go fetch and pull out the complete text from a handful of specific web pages and academic paper documents I already have links to, all in one combined batch.
rows.expert: Need a web search for recent technical writeups on a method, plus batch full-text extraction from a set of specific article URLs and academic PDFs.

rows.synonym: I have a small number of hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images and just need a simple way to detect tissue areas, extract patches, and normalize the staining to build a quick deep-learning dataset — nothing as involved as multiplexed spatial protein analysis.
rows.plain: I have a few full-slide microscope images stained with the standard two-color pathology stain, and I just need an easy way to figure out where the actual tissue is on the slide, cut it into smaller square pieces, and adjust the color staining so it's consistent across images, in order to quickly build a dataset for a deep-learning model. I don't need anything as heavy-duty as a full multi-marker spatial protein-mapping analysis.
rows.expert: Need lightweight H&E WSI tissue detection, tiling, and stain normalization for a deep-learning dataset — no multiplexed spatial-proteomics workflow needed.

rows.synonym: I need to store a very large multi-dimensional array so that I can read and write chunks of it in parallel, ideally directly to cloud object storage, while remaining smoothly compatible with downstream numerical array and labeled-array analysis tools.
rows.plain: I need to store a huge grid of numbers with many dimensions, in a way that lets different parts of it be read and written at the same time by multiple processes, ideally saved directly to cloud-based storage. It also needs to work well afterward with the standard numerical and labeled-array analysis tools I already use.
rows.expert: Need chunked, parallel-read/write storage for a large multi-dimensional array, ideally direct to cloud object storage, interoperable with standard array/labeled-array analysis tools.

rows.synonym: I want to construct a clinical deep-learning pipeline that predicts in-hospital mortality from ICU electronic health record data structured like the MIMIC-III database, covering everything from the raw patient dataset through task definition, model training, and evaluation metrics.
rows.plain: I want to build a deep-learning pipeline for predicting whether intensive-care patients will die during their hospital stay, using electronic medical-record data structured like a well-known public intensive-care patient database. I want this to cover the whole process — starting from the raw patient records, through defining exactly what's being predicted, training the model, and measuring how well it performs.
rows.expert: Need an end-to-end clinical DL pipeline for in-hospital mortality prediction on MIMIC-III-structured ICU EHR data: task definition, model training, and evaluation.

rows.synonym: I have several already-built gene trees saved in the standard Newick tree-text format, and I want to compare their topologies using Robinson-Foulds distances, reconcile them against a species tree to identify gene duplication and loss events, and render a publication-quality figure of the results.
rows.plain: I have several evolutionary trees for individual genes, already built and saved in a common plain-text tree format, and I want to compare how similar their branching patterns are using a standard tree-difference measure, then compare them against an overall species tree to find out where genes were duplicated or lost during evolution, and finally produce a nicely formatted figure showing the result.
rows.expert: Need Robinson-Foulds topology comparison across Newick-format gene trees, gene-tree/species-tree reconciliation to identify duplication/loss events, and a publication-quality tree figure.

rows.synonym: An editor has asked me to peer-review a submitted paper, and I need help organizing a rigorous, evidence-based evaluation covering its methodology, statistical approach, and reproducibility, while keeping the unpublished material strictly confidential.
rows.plain: A journal editor has asked me to critically review a paper that hasn't been published yet, and I need help putting together a careful, well-supported evaluation that looks closely at how the study was conducted, how the statistics were done, and whether the results could be reproduced by someone else — all while making sure the unpublished content stays completely confidential and isn't shared anywhere.
rows.expert: Need to structure a rigorous peer-review assessment (methods, statistics, reproducibility) for a submitted manuscript, maintaining strict confidentiality of unpublished content.

rows.synonym: I have a neural-network training loop weighed down with repetitive code for checkpointing, logging, and multi-GPU coordination, and I want to restructure it into a clean, modular trainer design that scales cleanly to distributed training, whether using data-parallel replication or sharded-parameter strategies.
rows.plain: I have code that trains a deep-learning model, but it's cluttered with a lot of repeated setup code for saving progress, recording logs, and coordinating across multiple graphics cards. I want to reorganize this into a clean, well-structured design — separating the model logic from the training-management logic — in a way that scales smoothly to running across many machines, using either a strategy that copies the model to each device or one that splits the model's parameters across devices.
rows.expert: Need to refactor a training loop (checkpointing/logging/multi-GPU boilerplate) into a modular trainer design that scales cleanly to distributed data-parallel or parameter-sharded training.

rows.synonym: I need to fit a generalized linear model and produce complete coefficient tables, standard errors, and diagnostic tests for non-constant error variance and serial correlation — the level of detailed statistical output required for a rigorous econometrics write-up.
rows.plain: I need to fit a standard regression-style statistical model and get a complete table of the estimated effect sizes with their uncertainty measures, plus formal checks for whether the error variability changes across observations and whether errors are correlated over time — the kind of thorough, detailed statistical reporting that a serious economics-style write-up would require.
rows.expert: Need a fitted GLM with full coefficient/SE tables and heteroskedasticity/autocorrelation diagnostic tests, at econometrics-reporting rigor.

rows.synonym: I want to package my bioinformatics pipeline as a workflow on the Latch platform, set the GPU and memory allocations for each individual task, launch it through their programmatic interface, and push the resulting run metadata into their structured data-tracking system.
rows.plain: I want to take my bioinformatics processing pipeline and package it up as a workflow that runs on the Latch platform, set how much graphics-processing power and memory each step of the pipeline should get, start the whole thing running through Latch's programmatic interface, and then send information about the completed run into Latch's structured record-keeping system.
rows.expert: Need to package a bioinformatics pipeline as a Latch workflow with per-task GPU/memory configuration, launch programmatically, and push run metadata to Latch's structured registry.

rows.synonym: I have 16S ribosomal RNA amplicon sequences and a sample-by-organism abundance table from several soil locations, and I want to calculate within-sample and between-sample diversity measures, run a permutational multivariate analysis of variance on the community differences across sites, and construct an ordination plot from the results.
rows.plain: I have gene-sequence data targeting a standard marker used to identify different microbes, along with a table showing how much of each type of organism is present in soil samples from several sites. I want to calculate how diverse each individual sample is, and how different the samples are from one another, run a statistical test for whether the microbial communities genuinely differ between sites, and produce a visual map that lays out how similar or different the samples are from each other.
rows.expert: Need alpha/beta diversity metrics from 16S amplicon abundance tables across soil sites, a PERMANOVA on between-site community differences, and an ordination plot.

rows.synonym: I'm preparing my manuscript for submission to a particular journal, and I need to confirm their actual current page limits, required sections, and official typesetting template files, instead of guessing based on an outdated template I found online, plus obtain a starting scaffold I can build my manuscript from.
rows.plain: I'm getting my paper ready to submit to a specific journal, and I need to check what that journal's current rules actually are — how many pages are allowed, which sections are required, and what formatting template files they want — rather than just guessing based on some old template I found somewhere online. I also want a basic starting document structure I can build my manuscript from.
rows.expert: Need to confirm a target journal's current page limits, required sections, and formatting template files (not an outdated template), plus an initial manuscript scaffold.

rows.synonym: I've trained a model locally and want to deploy it as a scalable web-accessible API, where GPU-backed containers spin up automatically on demand, without me having to manage my own container-orchestration cluster or write container build definitions.
rows.plain: I've already trained a model on my own machine, and I want to make it available online as a scalable web service that other programs can call, where computing resources with graphics processing automatically start up when needed and shut down when not, without me having to set up or manage my own cluster-management system or write low-level container build instructions myself.
rows.expert: Need to deploy a locally trained model as a scalable, on-demand GPU-backed web API endpoint, with no self-managed orchestration cluster or container build authoring required.

rows.synonym: I have the Fc region sequence of an antibody and want to scan it for N-linked glycosylation sequons and pinpoint likely O-linked glycosylation hotspots, since we're modifying the glycosylation pattern to enhance antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity while reducing immunogenicity.
rows.plain: I have the sequence of the tail-end constant region of an antibody, and I want to scan it for the specific short sequence patterns that mark where sugar chains attach to a particular type of amino acid, and also identify likely spots where a different type of sugar attachment might occur. We're changing this sugar-decoration pattern to make the antibody better at triggering immune cells to kill target cells, while also making it less likely to trigger an unwanted immune reaction against the antibody itself.
rows.expert: Need N-linked glycosylation sequon scanning and O-glycosylation hotspot prediction on an antibody Fc sequence, to guide glycoengineering for improved ADCC and reduced immunogenicity.

rows.synonym: I'm working on a machine-learning project involving protein sequence-based language models, and I want to find well-curated datasets, pretrained models, and interactive demos on a major public machine-learning model-sharing hub that are specifically relevant to biology, rather than doing broad, generic searching.
rows.plain: I'm working on a machine-learning project that uses language-style models trained on protein sequences, and I want to find good-quality, well-organized datasets, already-trained models, and interactive demo tools hosted on a big public online hub where people share machine-learning resources — specifically the ones relevant to biology, rather than just doing a broad general search.
rows.expert: Need curated, biology-specific datasets, pretrained models, and demos on a major public ML model hub for a protein-language-model project, rather than generic hub-wide search.

rows.synonym: I need to draft a CONSORT-compliant results-report template for our randomized trial's synthetic dataset, organized around the required reporting checklist items, ready for our statistician and clinical lead to review and finalize.
rows.plain: I need to put together a draft results report for our randomized trial's practice dataset, organized around the standard set of items that reporting guidelines require trials to cover, so it's ready for our statistician and clinical lead to check over and finish.
rows.expert: Need a CONSORT-compliant results-report scaffold for the trial's synthetic dataset, structured by required checklist items, for statistician/clinical-lead review and finalization.

rows.synonym: I have a set of nodes and connections representing protein-protein interactions, and I want to calculate centrality measures, identify communities within the network, and find the shortest path between two particular proteins.
rows.plain: I have a list of proteins and the interactions between them, treated as a network of connected points. I want to calculate which proteins are most central or influential in this network, find groups of proteins that cluster tightly together, and determine the shortest connecting path between two specific proteins.
rows.expert: Need centrality computation, community detection, and shortest-path analysis on a protein-protein interaction network.

rows.synonym: I need to design and review a multi-panel figure for my manuscript, making sure the colors are distinguishable for colorblind readers, the error bars are clearly and honestly labeled, and the axes don't visually exaggerate the effect, before submitting it to the journal.
rows.plain: I need to design and carefully check a figure made of several panels for my paper before I submit it to a journal, making sure the colors chosen can still be told apart by readers with color blindness, the bars showing uncertainty or error are clearly and honestly labeled so no one is misled, and the axis scales don't make the effect look bigger than it really is.
rows.expert: Need to design and audit a multi-panel manuscript figure for colorblind-accessible palette choice, honest uncertainty-bar labeling, and non-exaggerating axis scaling, prior to journal submission.

rows.synonym: I'm assembling the reference list for my manuscript and need to search for a set of papers, cross-check their author, journal, and publication-year details against the original sources, and produce accurate, duplicate-free entries in a standard structured bibliography format.
rows.plain: I'm putting together the list of references for my paper, and I need to search for a specific set of papers, double-check that the author names, journal, and publication year are all correct by comparing against the original sources, and then produce a clean, accurate set of reference entries, with no duplicates, in a standard structured format that citation-management tools can read.
rows.expert: Need literature search with source-verified author/journal/year metadata, producing accurate, deduplicated entries in a standard structured bibliography format.

rows.synonym: For a gene I'm interested in, I want to identify which individuals in the 1000 Genomes Project cohort carry homozygous missense variants in that gene, along with their gnomAD population allele frequencies and AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores.
rows.plain: For a specific gene, I want to find which people, in a well-known public reference cohort of sequenced genomes, carry two copies of a protein-changing variant in that gene, along with how common each variant is across a large population-frequency database, and a computationally predicted score for how likely each variant is to be harmful.
rows.expert: Need to identify 1000 Genomes Project individuals homozygous for missense variants in a gene of interest, with gnomAD allele frequencies and AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores.

rows.synonym: I want to build a parameterized quantum circuit and optimize its parameters with gradient-descent methods to solve a small eigenvalue problem, using automatic differentiation so I can later switch freely between a simulator and different physical hardware backends.
rows.plain: I want to build a quantum computing circuit whose settings can be adjusted, and train those settings using a step-by-step optimization method to solve a small problem involving finding a system's characteristic energy values. I want the training to use automatic calculus tools that compute how to adjust the settings, so that later I can freely switch between running this on a simulated quantum computer and running it on different actual quantum hardware.
rows.expert: Need a variational quantum circuit trained via gradient descent (with autodiff) to solve a small eigenvalue problem, portable across simulator and hardware backends.

rows.synonym: I'm writing a custom workflow-language module with its own task and data-flow logic, and I need help setting up tests using a dedicated pipeline-testing framework and configuring it to run correctly on our high-performance computing job-scheduling cluster.
rows.plain: I'm writing a custom module in a workflow-description language, with its own logic for defining processing steps and how data flows between them, and I need help setting up automated tests for it using a testing tool built for this kind of pipeline, and configuring it so it runs correctly on our shared computing cluster that schedules jobs.
rows.expert: Need to set up pipeline-level tests for a custom workflow-language module (with its own process/channel logic) using a dedicated testing framework, configured for our HPC job-scheduling cluster.

rows.synonym: I want to fetch a pretrained language model, run it through a text-classification workflow on my own dataset, and then fine-tune it using a standard training loop with customized training settings.
rows.plain: I want to download an already-trained language-understanding model, use it to sort my own collection of text into categories, and then further train it on my data using a standard step-by-step training process, with my own custom settings for how that training runs.
rows.expert: Need to download a pretrained LM, run zero-shot text classification on a custom dataset, then fine-tune via a standard training loop with custom training arguments.

rows.synonym: I need to write and locally simulate a liquid-handling protocol for our Opentrons Flex robot, including runtime parameters and control of a temperature module, before it ever runs on the actual physical deck.
rows.plain: I need to write a set of instructions for our Opentrons Flex liquid-handling robot that tells it how to move and mix liquids, including adjustable settings chosen at run time and control over a temperature-controlling attachment, and I want to test the whole thing in a local simulation first, before it actually touches the real equipment.
rows.expert: Need to author and locally simulate an Opentrons Flex liquid-handling protocol, including runtime parameters and temperature-module control, prior to physical deck execution.
